summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 1, part 166) in which two young characters, Ange and the narrator, prepare to go fugitive. The narrator recalls advice on packing light, then watches Ange pack a courier bag with a minimal set of clothes and toiletries. Ange also plans to protect the data on her Xbox hard-drive by emailing an encrypted image of it to herself through a Pirate Party account before leaving. The narrator reflects on the impending separation, which may be long or permanent, and the excerpt ends mid-scene as Ange adds condoms to the bag.
one_line: Ange and the narrator prepare to go fugitive, packing light and emailing encrypted drive backups before leaving for LA.
key_facts: The narrator says every ounce added to a pack cuts into the shoulders, becoming a ton over a million steps.
Ange plans to pack three t-shirts, a pair of pants, a pair of shorts, three changes of underwear, three pairs of socks and a sweater.
Ange says never take more than three days' worth of clothes and that stains can be rinsed out in the sink.
Ange chooses a ballistic nylon courier bag that goes across her chest and slings diagonally across her back.
Ange's hard-drive data is encrypted, which the narrator says is standard with ParanoidXbox.
The narrator tells Ange to leave the Xbox behind because there will be plenty of them in LA.
Ange is told to create a Pirate Party account and email an image of her hard-drive to herself.
The emailed hard-drive image will take a couple of hours to upload through her neighbor's WiFi network and reach Sweden.
Ange plans to stick her toothbrush in the morning before heading down to Civic Center.
The narrator reflects that the next day they will go away, maybe for a long time or forever.
Ange takes condoms from her bedside table and stows them in the courier bag before giving the narrator a slap on the ass.
The narrator's message to Masha, signed M1k3y, says 'Tomorrow'.
The excerpt opens with a message promising 'the most fun you will have all year, guaranteed' and ends with 'Believe.'
